turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?

Mrs. Kalinowski, honest question, mother to teacher. Don't you think a smart kid like Owen would never write a line that isn't in the play? If he'd really written it, he'd know. So doesn't the fake quote actually prove somebody else, not him, wrote it? Argue that for me, as my ally, I'd like to understand how you'd build the case against him.

Meredith doesn't take the bait. She stays on Owen and makes Hale show the evidence.

"Ally? I'm not your ally, Ms. Hale. I'm his mother. And I'm not going to argue your case for you so you can hear it back in your own voice."

She sets her bag on the chair beside her and doesn't sit down.

"You say the quote isn't in the play. Fine. So a quote is wrong. Plenty of students misquote Shakespeare from memory, and I'd bet most of your Grade 12s have never opened Act 3 in their lives. A wrong line tells me he didn't check a citation. It doesn't tell me who typed the sentence."

"I'm not interested in what a fake quote might prove. I'm interested in what you have that's dated. You told me the essay was flagged. You haven't told me when the file was created, what it contains, or who else has seen it. So show me."
